chapter_outcomes: The United Nations (UN).  • Origins and development of the UN, including its 1945  charter.  • Role and significance of the UN to include the Security  Council, General Assembly, Economic and Social Council,  International Court of Justice including their strengths and  weaknesses.
Role and significance of NATO including its changing role,  particularly since the end of the Cold War, and strengths and  weaknesses.
International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.  • Role and significance of these institutions, including their  strengths and weaknesses.

Significance of how global economic governance deals with the  issue of poverty, including:  • The North-South divide and other measurements to include  world-systems theory, dependency, orthodox and alternative  measurements of poverty.

The World Trade Organisation (WTO) and G7/G8 and G20.  • Classical economic development theory, structural theory,  neo-classical development theory.  • Role and significance of these institutions, including their  strengths and weaknesses.

The ways and extent to which these institutions address and  resolve contemporary global issues, such as those involving  conflict, poverty, human rights and the environment.
